original_question: If K is an infinite field whose absolute Galois group GK is finitely generated as a topological group, must K be ample?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1 (Introduction): whether every infinite field K with finitely generated absolute Galois group G_K is ample.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct conjectural implication, the right ambient object (an infinite field K), and the intended Galois-theoretic hypothesis. The added phrase 'as a topological group' is appropriate because G_K is a profinite group.
missing_details: Spell out G_K as the absolute Galois group Gal(K^sep/K).
Make explicit that 'finitely generated' means finitely generated as a profinite/topological group.
Define 'ample' in the paper's sense: every smooth geometrically integral K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points.
Optionally record the paper's equivalent reformulation from Proposition 1.2: K is existentially closed in K((t)).
State the curve-quantifier explicitly so the problem is fully stand-alone.
refined_question: Let K be an infinite field, and let G_K=Gal(K^sep/K) be its absolute Galois group endowed with the Krull topology. If G_K is finitely generated as a profinite (equivalently, topological) group, must K be ample; that is, must every smooth geometrically integral curve C over K with C(K) nonempty have infinitely many K-rational points?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the same hypotheses on K, must K be existentially closed in the Laurent series field K((t))?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's target: it matches Conjecture 1.1 in the introduction. The only real incompleteness is that the notation G_K and the meaning of 'ample' are left implicit. Proposition 1.2 is the paper-explicit equivalence that lets one restate ampleness as existential closedness in K((t)), so that is the only alternate formulation included. I therefore kept the question at exactly the same scope as the paper's conjecture and only unpacked the hidden definitions needed to make it self-contained.
